verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. All three clauses are present, and the amplitude clause is stronger in Lean than in the paper. T_d = e^{M_d} + 10 is Parameters.dropLength (= Real.exp c.m + 10, same constant, same exponential) and X_R = 110(C P_*)^{10} is matchingRadius/resetRadius with Xi = 110. The paper's P_* > e^{T_d} appears as amplitudeThreshold m ≤ P with amplitudeThreshold m = Real.exp (Real.exp m + 11) + 1 (OutgoingEntranceCone.lean:1809), which is exactly e^{T_d+1} + 1, since the file itself proves dropLength + 1 = Real.exp m + 11 at :1855. Direction checked: e^{T_d+1} + 1 > e^{T_d}, so the Lean hypothesis implies the paper's and not conversely. It is assumed exactly where the paper assumes it: at chosen_parameters_bounds (:1845), exists_ordered_preliminary_bounds (:1869), OutgoingCone.exists_ordered_clean_cone (:460) and exists_ordered_profile_cone (:503); and it is met by the profile actually constructed, since PreparedOutgoing.exists_prepared sets P := max 2 (amplitudeThreshold M) at PreparedOutgoing.lean:39 with core.m = M. The weaker-looking hypothesis Real.exp (c.dropLength + 1) ≤ c.P ^ 2 seen at OutgoingEntranceCone.lean:987, 1037, 1050 and OutgoingCone.lean:257, 408 is not a substitute for the clause: it is derived from amplitudeThreshold m ≤ P at OutgoingEntranceCone.lean:1853.
